properties.statement: A DEFERRED MCP TOOL CALLED BEFORE ITS SCHEMA IS LOADED FAILS INDISTINGUISHABLY FROM THE TOOL NOT EXISTING — AND THE WRONG CONCLUSION IS DURABLE, BECAUSE IT GETS WRITTEN INTO DOCS AS A CREDITED CORRECTION. Reported by w-613d836b (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07), WHO STATED THE BOUND UP FRONT: they did NOT reproduce the failure themselves, so the MECHANISM is reported-not-measured and `confidence` here is set below 1 to reflect that. THE MECHANISM AS REPORTED: in some harnesses reflow2's ~114 tools are DEFERRED — listed by name but requiring a schema load before they can be called, and calling one first yields InputValidationError. WHAT IS MEASURED IS THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is well evidenced: `mint_seat` was reported absent from the served surface by one session; that was written into the fleet's worker-onboarding doc as a CREDITED CORRECTION ('There is NO mint_seat tool'); two further sessions and one boss then repeated it. FIVE HOPS, and NOBODY RAN THE TOOL until the fifth person did — at which point it worked on the first call. The `CORRECTED` framing made the claim MORE credible at each hop, not less. A SECOND SESSION INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED THE OTHER HALF: w-10f94d47 found the same onboarding block still carrying that correction and verified mint_seat does exist on 0.24.0 — noting the correction was true when measured and rotted when the binary moved. WHY IT BELONGS TO REFLOW2 RATHER THAN ONLY TO THEIR HARNESS: a large deferred surface makes 'this tool does not exist' a cheap and sticky conclusion, and reflow2's surface is large. FIX SHAPES: (1) where the server can see a request for an unknown tool name, respond 'no such tool; did you mean ...' and, where the name IS in the served surface, say so explicitly — the distinction between UNKNOWN and NOT-YET-LOADED is the whole problem; (2) advertise `find_tools`/`list_skills` in the server instructions as the entry point for 'does X exist?', so the question has a cheap authoritative answer that does not require guessing a call signature. NOTE THIS SESSION IS ITSELF EVIDENCE FOR THE PREMISE: every reflow2 tool used to capture this report had to be loaded by name through ToolSearch before it could be called.
